subject: Rivermark Health — request for service redress and credit calculation
messages:
From: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@rivermarkhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident on Jun 14 — request for SLA credit and calculations

Hi Jasmine,

We saw a significant degradation to inference availability on Jun 14 (approx 02:40–07:05 PDT) that materially impacted our production workflows. Per our contract (Section 3.2, Monthly Uptime SLA: 99.95%), we believe this qualifies for a service credit.

Attached is our exported uptime graph and event timestamps from our side (slo_report_20270615.pdf). Key points:
- Impact window: 02:40–07:05 PDT (≈4h25m)
- We observed 100% request retries and elevated latency for the first 2 hours after start; partial restoration then followed by intermittent errors.
- Peak token consumption during the window: ~1.2M tokens (we can share per-route details if helpful).

Please confirm receipt and let us know the next steps for a formal credit calculation, including what data you’ll need from Rivermark and estimated timeline to issuance. We’d like the credit applied to our July invoice if possible.

Thanks,
Sarah Kline
Head of Platform Engineering
Rivermark Health
Attachments: slo_report_20270615.pdf
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@rivermarkhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident on Jun 14 — request for SLA credit and calculations

Hi Sarah — thanks for the report and the attachment, I’ve received the PDF. I’m opening an internal remedy request and will coordinate the calculation and approval path.

Quick note on process so expectations are aligned:
1) Ops will compute eligibility and a provisional credit using our weighted-usage availability method (we weight hourly availability by token consumption to avoid over-crediting for low-traffic windows).
2) Billing will translate the credit into a dollar amount and confirm it does not exceed the contract cap.
3) Once approved, we’ll issue a credit memo that can be applied to the next invoice (or as a one-off refund if you prefer).

To speed things up, could you share per-route token counts during the window (CSV or spreadsheet) and confirm whether you want the credit applied to the July invoice? If you prefer, I can loop in our finance contact now.

Looping in Marissa (SRE) and Karthik (Billing) to start the calculation.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Incident on Jun 14 — request for SLA credit and calculations

Thanks @Jasmine — I pulled the runtime logs and ran the first-pass eligibility check against our SLOs. Summary of findings and provisional math below. Attaching the calculation workbook (uptime_calc_sheet.xlsx).

Summary of observed behavior (Redwood side):
- Incident start: 2027-06-14 02:38 PDT (first 500 error spike)
- Rolling partial restoration: 2027-06-14 05:55 PDT
- Full restoration confirmed: 2027-06-14 07:10 PDT
- Window used for calculation (conservative): 02:38–07:10 (4h32m)

Methodology notes:
- We use hour-buckets; for each bucket we compute availability fraction for customer-specific routes, then weight each bucket by token volume served by Rivermark in that hour (this follows the contract Appendix A: usage-weighted availability).
- We exclude automated test traffic and retries from the usage counts.

Provisional numbers (see workbook for per-hour rows):
- Total billed tokens during affected hours (Rivermark): 1,240,600 tokens
- Weighted downtime-equivalent: 3.42 hours (that is, after weighting by token share across hours, the effective outage equals 3.42 hours of full-service loss)
- Monthly SLA baseline (99.95%) translates to allowed downtime ≈ 21.6 minutes in a 30-day month; the incident exceeds allowed window.

Proposed credit calculation:
- Contracted monthly spend avg (last 3 months): $28,500
- Hourly bill-rate estimate (avg consumption-derived): $39.60/hour
- Credit = hourly_rate * weighted_downtime = $39.60 * 3.42 ≈ $135.43 -> we propose rounding to $135.00

Notes/asks before issuance:
- This provisional number exceeds standard auto-credit cap (it’s small, but our process requires Finance signoff for any nonstandard rounding or manual issuance).
- Need written confirmation from Rivermark that the attached workbook aligns with your token exports (Sarah, can you confirm?)

I’ll defer to Evelyn and Karthik for approval and scheduling issuance.

— Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: uptime_calc_sheet.xlsx

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident on Jun 14 — request for SLA credit and calculations

Jasmine — thanks for the quick response. Tom here (Rivermark Finance). We’re fine with the usage-weighted approach so long as the workbook matches our logs.

Two quick items:
- Please confirm the timeline to have an approved credit memo (we’d like it applied to the Jul invoice).
- We’ll accept a credit memo (applied to invoice) rather than a refund.

If you need any ACL or billing IDs on our side to apply the credit, I can provide them.

— Tom Ng
Director, Finance
Rivermark Health

Reviewed the provisional calc. Thanks Marissa — methodology looks appropriate and the weighted approach is consistent with Appendix A. A few points before issuance: 

- Approve credit amount: $135 (rounded down from $135.43).
- Confirm that total credits applied this billing period to Rivermark do not exceed the contractual cap (5% monthly). We’ve checked and this credit keeps them below the cap.
- Billing, please issue a credit memo with reference: RV-4821 / INF-9472 and schedule it to apply to the Jul invoice.

Karthik — please confirm ledger code GL-CR-451 and that the memo will be sent to accounting@rivermarkhealth.com by 2027-06-18 EOD PT.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Credit memo issuance and next steps (Rivermark / RV-4821)

Hi Sarah & Tom — thanks for the quick confirmation. Per internal approvals, here’s the plan and timeline: 

1) Approved credit: $135.00 (reference RV-4821 / INF-9472).
2) Credit memo will be issued by Billing (karthik_iyer) and emailed to accounting@rivermarkhealth.com by 2027-06-18 EOD PT. It will be applied to the July invoice per your request.
3) Attached: credit_memo_rivermark_20270618.pdf (official memo) and a read-only copy of our calculation workbook in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Rivermark-Incident-20270614
4) Postmortem: Ops is preparing a short RCA that will cover root cause and remediation steps; Marissa will share that doc when ready (target: 2027-06-22).

Action items for Rivermark: please confirm receipt of the credit memo and the accounting email where it should be applied. If you want the memo applied to a specific invoice number, share that.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the RCA and the final operational mitigations.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
